question: Does the single transfer-completeness review plugin improve outcomes under a controlled paired request protocol?

fixed_conditions.changed_component: Only the review plugin registration is removed in off; all six other plugins remain.

pairing_definition.model_request_coupling: Within one task/trial pair, the nth identical model request shares one response across off/on; repeated requests within the same arm still get a fresh occurrence. Both arms branch on changed input.

interpretation: Within a task/trial pair, the nth identical model request shares one response across on/off; a changed request branches. Attribution verifies the first changed actor request occurs after the actual review intervention. This controls shared-prefix stochastic variation, but is not the ordinary independent production protocol.
limitations: A single plugin, checkpoint, benchmark and request-coupling protocol were tested. This does not establish that every DSH plugin or search strategy improves performance.
These are newly measured paired outcomes; the original V4 test score of 96/120 (80.00%) is retained separately.
The changed-request suffix remains stochastic; the 342 pairs do not represent 342 independent evolution searches.
No previously successful episode was retried just to improve score; original historical benchmark scores were not overwritten.
Numeric pair outcomes and aggregate checks are published; raw conversations and request bodies are not.
